title: Ignore/allow hosts semantics in _ignore_connection
answers: How do ignore_hosts and allow_hosts work?
Why are Host header/SNI only checked when server.address is known?
body:
`mitmproxy/addons/next_layer.py:NextLayer._ignore_connection` reads `ctx.options` (ignore_hosts/allow_hosts) directly, not the compiled lists from `configure`.
- Returns False early if neither option set, and for the WireGuard DNS special case 10.0.0.53:53.
- Candidates `host:port`: `server.peername`, `server.address`; only if `server.address` is known also HTTP Host header (`_get_host_header`, appends port), SNI from ClientHello (`_get_client_hello`), and `client.sni`. Deliberate: without a destination address an ignored connection couldn't be forwarded upstream.
- Order: allow_hosts set and no candidate matches -> ignored; then any ignore_hosts match -> ignored; else not ignored.
- Evaluated first in `_next_layer`, so it overrides reverse/explicit proxy modes.
